identity.title: On the Identification of Temporal Causal Representation with Instantaneous Dependence

problem.claim: Identify latent causal processes from time-series observations when latent variables have both time-delayed and instantaneous relations.

gap.claim: Existing methods generally exclude instantaneous relations; methods addressing them require latent interventions or grouped observations, which are difficult to obtain in real-world settings.

contributions.claim: Proposes IDOL, an identification framework imposing sparse time-delayed and instantaneous latent influences.
Establishes identifiability results using sufficient variability, sparse influence, and contextual time-series information.
Combines temporally variational inference with gradient-based sparsity regularization to estimate latent variables and identify the latent causal process.

stated_novelty.claim: The framework targets instantaneous latent dynamics without the interventions or observation grouping required by some recent approaches, using sparse influence and contextual information.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that simulation experiments illustrate identification of the latent causal process.
The authors report that evaluations on multiple human-motion forecasting benchmarks with instantaneous dependencies indicate effectiveness in real-world settings.

narrative_sequence.summary: Temporal causal representation learning is introduced, with instantaneous latent relations identified as a limitation of most methods.
Some methods handle instantaneous causality but depend on difficult-to-obtain latent interventions or grouped observations.
IDOL addresses the setting through sparse instantaneous and delayed influences, with identifiability based on variability and contextual information.
The theory is operationalized with temporally variational inference and gradient-based sparsity regularization.
Reported results cover simulations and human-motion forecasting benchmarks.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns the identifiability assumptions with corresponding modeling mechanisms: sparse influence is used in both the theoretical framework and the sparsity regularizer.

lessons.interpretation: Making assumptions visibly operative can connect a theoretical claim to an implementable method.
lessons.application: When presenting a structured latent-variable method, map each identifiability assumption to an explicit architectural component or optimization term.
lessons.exception: This mapping may be unsuitable when an assumption is only analytical and has no faithful computational surrogate.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact sufficient-variability condition, sparsity levels, or identifiability scope.
The reported experiments do not provide quantitative metrics, baselines, sample sizes, or ablations.
The real-world benchmark results are described as indicating effectiveness, but the decisive comparative conditions are not stated.
